financial_summary: Northern Oil and Gas, Inc. is a mid-cap energy business with a $2.7B market cap on $2.5B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +16% over the past three years and +25% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are contracting by -2.4pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 15% against a 8% cost of capital, a 7-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $1.5B in free cash flow — roughly 61 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 38.84× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 9.7× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Management returns a meaningful 8.7% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 2.9% of the shares.

ESG-driven capital flight and stranded asset risk — tightening climate policy and investor mandates raise the cost of capital and risk leaving reserves permanently in the ground.
Geopolitical supply shocks — wars, sanctions, and OPEC decisions create volatility that no hedging programme can fully neutralise.
